title: Cross-sku MIG clock interlock: kernel prioritization and attention tiling for H100/L40S/A10
creator: Asha Menon
description: Background: multi-tenant inference workloads on H100/L40S/A10 show volatile tail latency during MIG consolidation and clock domain shifts. Current kernel selection heuristics assume static clock/perf profiles and do not account for transient P2P/NVLink contention or mixed quantized/FP16 execution paths. Goal: implement a cross-sku clock-interlock and kernel prioritization layer plus an attention-tiling policy that adapts prefill/decode scheduling to MIG partitioning and real-time clock governors. Success metrics: 95th percentile latency reduction of 15-25% on mixed small/long-sequence workloads across MIG partitions; token cost neutral or improved; no regression in throughput for long-batch offline workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel router uses live clock and MIG fragmentation signals to rank candidate kernels before scheduling
Attention tiler adjusts tile size and KV alignment to reduce L2 thrash on L40S without increasing decode latency > 5%
Prefill/decode interleave window introduced to avoid clock-rebalance stalls during MIG reconfigure and reduces 95th latency by >=15% in benchmark suite
Automated telemetry demonstrates correct fallback to a quantized-kernel-fusion path on A10 when H100/L40S capacity constrained
End-to-end e2e perf tests and canary on dedicated pool show no increase in error rate or CPU OOMs
work_notes: 2025-01-18: RFC written; linked design doc with microbenchmarks. Trade-offs considered: aggressive prefill batching vs latency-sensitive interleaving. Decision: hybrid interleaving with dynamic cutover thresholds.
2025-01-22: Infra experiment on staging with synthetic chat workload; observed 28% 95th latency spike when MIG fragmentation >60% during background training noise.
2025-01-25: Implemented clock-interlock event listener in runtime and exposed telemetry flag runtime.clock_interlock.enabled (off by default).

2025-01-29: Prototyped kernel-ranking heuristic that weights (kernel_peak_bw, current_device_clock, nvlink_util, mig_fragment_score). Initial synthetic results: 12% 95th reduction on H100-only trials.
2025-02-01: L40S attention tiler patch submitted; adjusts attn_tile to favor smaller tiles when L2 miss rate > 18%. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921

2025-02-03: End-to-end benchmark ran against mixed H100/L40S/A10 pool with prefill+decode interleave window set to 40ms; 95th improved by 17% and token cost decreased 3% on median. Noted small throughput regression on long-batch profiles (~4%).

Next steps: add NVLink P2P fallback handshake to kernel router; integrate autoswitch thresholds from telemetry; create canary rollout plan for dedicated customers and a gated feature flag for runtime-1.21 release.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive kernel switching can increase warmup overhead. Mitigation: add hysteresis and min residency time per kernel selection.
Risk: L40S micro-tiling may regress throughput on long static batches. Mitigation: enable tiler only when L2 miss + latency SLO signals are present.
Risk: MIG reconfigure race during runtime may cause transient errors. Mitigation: gate reconfigure events via interlock and drain inflight prefill windows before topology changes.
qa_plan: Add unit tests for kernel router ranking weights and simulated clock events
Run full perf suite on multi-sku lab (H100/L40S/A10) with and without background NVSwitch load
Canary rollout to dedicated pool group 'perf-canary-02' with telemetry thresholds for automatic rollback
